introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: three hours fifteen minutes.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer ALL the THREE QUESTIONS. Question ONE carries thirty-four marks and the rest carry thirty-three marks each.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Photos, Graph Paper and outline map (where relevant).

Tableau de la Q2 recopié du sujet : les nombres imprimés sans virgule (« 1,412467 », « 855334 », « 712550 »...) sont transcrits avec des séparateurs réguliers (1,412,467 ; 855,334 ; 712,550...). Valeurs arrondies à une décimale (les colonnes sommées donnent 99,9 à cause des arrondis, 100 en valeurs exactes). Une autre lecture (part des hommes dans chaque tranche d'âge) est possible mais ne permet pas de tracer une pyramide.

Q2(b)(i) : segmentation imposée par le sujet (jeunes 0-19, adultes 20-59, vieux 60+) : jeunes 10,635,399 ; adultes 7,809,416 ; vieux 961,285 ; rapport de dépendance = (10,635,399 + 961,285) / 7,809,416 x 100 = 148,5 environ (recalculé par script). Le sujet ne précise pas si le résultat se donne en pourcentage ou pour 100 : le corrigé donne les deux formulations.

Les explications générales (immigration, dépendance, problèmes de la jeunesse) sont des réponses modèles sans statistique autre que celles du tableau imprimé ; à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) i) Complete the blanks spaces in the table indicating percentage of male and female. **(6.5 marks)**

ii) Using a population pyramid present the male and female data calculated in percentages **(9.5 marks)**

iii) state one advantage and one demerit of the technique used above in a)(ii) **(3 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Completing the table (6.5 marks).** Each percentage is the share of one age group in the total of its own sex:

% of male = (number of males in the age group / total males) x 100, with total males = 9,599,224;

% of female = (number of females in the age group / total females) x 100, with total females = 9,806,876.

Example: 0-4 males = 1,662,298 / 9,599,224 x 100 = 17.3 %; 0-4 females = 1,624,936 / 9,806,876 x 100 = 16.6 %.

(The percentages are rounded to one decimal place, so each column adds to 99.9 instead of 100.) Marks: method shown (1); the 30 values correct (about 4.5); totals 100 (1).

**(ii) The population pyramid (9.5 marks).**
1. Draw a vertical axis in the centre with the 15 age groups, in order from 0-4 at the bottom to 70+ at the top, each bar the same height.
2. Draw the horizontal scale on both sides of the central axis from 0 to 18 % (for example 1 cm = 2 %); males to the LEFT, females to the RIGHT.
3. Draw a bar for every age group on each side, with a length equal to its percentage (for example 0-4: 17.3 % on the left, 16.6 % on the right).
4. Label the age groups, the scale, the sexes (key), and give a title and the source.

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2024-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

**Description of the shape (for extra credit).** Very wide base (the 0-4 group is the biggest, 17.3 % and 16.6 %) narrowing quickly to a narrow top: the sides are concave and the pyramid is triangular. This is the shape of a young population with a high birth rate, a high death rate and a low proportion of old people (only about 5 % are aged 60 and over). From 20-24 upwards females are slightly more numerous (for example 8.9 % of males against 10.0 % of females in 20-24), while males slightly dominate the childrens groups.

**(iii) Advantage and demerit (3 marks).**
- *Advantage:* a pyramid shows at a glance the age and sex structure of a population, so the shape reveals the birth rate, death rate, dependent groups and the effects of migration; it allows an easy comparison between countries or years (using percentages).
- *Demerit:* it takes time and care to draw and the exact values are hard to read from the bars; the open-ended top group (70+) cannot be drawn to scale, and it shows only the structure, not the causes (migration or mortality) behind it.

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) i) Calculate the dependency ratio for the population using this segmentation of the population (youth 0-19, adults 20-59 and old 60+). **(4 marks)**

ii) Explain why the actual dependency ratio might be higher than the result obtained above. **(3 marks)**

iii) How may immigration influence dependency ratio. **(3 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Calculation (4 marks).** Dependency ratio = (youth + old) / adults x 100.

- Youth (0-19) = 3,287,234 + 2,783,459 + 2,394,671 + 2,170,035 = 10,635,399
- Adults (20-59) = 7,809,416 (the eight groups from 20-24 to 55-59)
- Old (60+) = 315,879 + 227,290 + 418,116 = 961,285

Dependants = 10,635,399 + 961,285 = 11,596,684.

Dependency ratio = 11,596,684 / 7,809,416 x 100 = **148.5** (about 148.5 dependants for every 100 adults aged 20-59; as a fraction, about 1.49).

Breakdown: youth dependency ratio = 10,635,399 / 7,809,416 x 100 = 136.2; old-age dependency ratio = 961,285 / 7,809,416 x 100 = 12.3. The burden is mainly due to children and young people.

**(ii) Why the real ratio may be higher (3 marks, any three points developed).**
- Not all adults aged 20-59 are working: many are unemployed or under-employed (a large informal and agricultural sector with low incomes), full-time students, sick or disabled, or at home, so the number of real producers is smaller than the 20-59 group.
- Some of the working-age adults have emigrated, so the number of adults who really support the dependants at home is lower.
- Many adults support, in addition, relatives of the extended family who are not counted as dependants in the table (for example orphans or other adults without income).
- Premature deaths of adults (for example from disease or accidents) reduce the number of workers.

**(iii) Influence of immigration (3 marks).**
- Immigrants are often young working adults (about 20-40 years), so they increase the adult group, which lowers the dependency ratio, and they add to production and taxes.
- If immigrants arrive as refugees or as families with many children and elderly relatives (as with refugees received in Cameroon from neighbouring countries), they increase the number of dependants and so raise the ratio, and add pressure on schools, health care and food supply.
- In the longer term the children born to the immigrants increase the youth group, while after some decades the immigrants age and raise the old-age group; so the effect depends on the age and sex of the migrants and on whether they find work.

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Identify two problems associated with youthful population and state two measures to overcome these problems. **(4 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Problems (1 mark each, any two).**
- *Unemployment and under-employment:* a large number of young people enter the labour market every year but there are not enough jobs, so many work in the informal sector or are idle.
- *Pressure on education and health services:* schools are overcrowded and lack classrooms and teachers; children's health care (vaccination, maternity care) is heavily demanded.
- *High dependency burden:* few workers support many children, so savings and investment are low and poverty persists.
- *Rural-urban migration, crime and social unrest* among unemployed youth; housing shortage in towns.

**Measures (1 mark each, any two).**
- Create jobs and promote youth entrepreneurship (small and medium enterprises, agricultural and agro-industrial projects, credit for young people).
- Provide vocational and technical training linked to the job market, and invest in more schools and teachers.
- Family planning and sensitisation to lower the birth rate in the long run.
- Develop rural areas (roads, electricity, markets) to slow down the movement of youth to towns.
